drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 63-year-old female admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.66, creatinine 0.9, hemoglobin 13.5, platelets 246, sodium 139, wbc 8.3; vitals dbp 75-80, heart_rate 82-87, map 91-96, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 124-129, spo2 97-98, temp 36.6-36.9
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Normal saline 1 L IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Anemia.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.86, hemoglobin 12.8, platelets 248, sodium 139, wbc 8.8; vitals dbp 75-80, heart_rate 82-87, map 92-97, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 124-130, spo2 97-98, temp 36.8-36.9
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Anemia. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 63-year-old female, length of stay 3 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Anemia. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
